text:
maya (Support): Customer reports intermittent 401s and says they can't find any request/trace id to share. They also use an Electron wrapper + internal proxy. asked for a minimal repro but want to be explicit about exactly what to ask for. any quick checklist?

ryan (Eng): Short checklist I send: 1) single curl that fails, 2) devtools HAR or electron net logs, 3) SDK logs showing request/response headers (INFO level), 4) a screenshot of the network request headers from the client's DevTools or the embedded webview console. Also ask if a reverse proxy/edge could be stripping headers (nginx / cloudflare).

maya (Support): can you paste the minimal curl snippet i should send? customer isn't dev-savvy.

ryan (Eng): Use this sample and ask them to replace the token and body — it forces the same path as their SDK call:

```
curl -i -v \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer REPLACE_WITH_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"input":"hello"}' \
  https://api.redwood-inference.example/v1/generate
```

ryan (Eng): Tell them to add `-D -` to print response headers and `--trace-ascii trace.txt` if curl is available. Example: `curl -i -D - --trace-ascii trace.txt ...`

jamie (Support-Lead): If they can't run curl, ask for: 1) a HAR export from the failing page (DevTools -> Network -> Export HAR), 2) a screenshot of raw request headers (right-click -> Copy -> Copy as cURL in Chrome works too). Also ask for timestamps (UTC) of the failing requests so we can match on our side.

maya (Support): electron/webview specifics: where do they find headers in an Electron app?

ryan (Eng): For Electron (or embedded webviews) instruct them: open the app with `--enable-logging --v=1` (if they have dev build) or run a sysdiagnose on mac: `sudo sysdiagnose -f ~/Desktop` and attach the bundle. Ask them to grep for `x-request-id` / `x-redwood-reqref` or `Authorization:` in `netlog`/`network` dumps. If they can't produce sysdiagnose, a lightweight step: reproduce the request, then in the app's DevTools Network tab, right-click the request -> "Copy" -> "Copy as cURL" and paste that.

maya (Support): good. what about our debug token?

ryan (Eng): If the customer can hit our debug endpoint (only for allowed customers), tell them the flow: click the "Share debug token" link in Console -> Support -> Create debug token, or we can generate one for them. If they give the debug token, include it in the thread and we can pull server-side traces without full HAR.

debug-bot: NOTE: If you include a debug token, also add the failing request UTC timestamp and the approximate request body. This helps trace archival logs.

jamie (Support-Lead): Final message I would send to customer (short):

"Can you please: 1) run this curl (replace API key) and paste the full output, or export a HAR/screenshot of the failing request; 2) include the exact UTC time(s) when the error happened; 3) if possible, attach a debug token from Console or the app sysdiagnose bundle. If you're behind a corporate proxy please tell us the proxy vendor/version. We'll correlate on our side once we have those pieces"

maya (Support): perfect — i'll send that now. :thumbsup:
